items.title: The Artin-Tate lemma: a subalgebra over which a finitely generated algebra is finite is of finite type
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The Artin-Tate lemma states that if R is Noetherian, S is a finitely generated R-algebra and T is an R-subalgebra over which S is finite, then T is of finite type over R (statement lines 12513-12519). The proof does not use determinants or integrality of the generators: it writes down the two finite generating sets, collects the finitely many structure constants into a subalgebra T', presents an auxiliary algebra S' over T' with those constants as relations, and uses the resulting surjection onto S together with Noetherianity of T' to conclude that T is finite over T' (proof lines 12521-12540). The construction of S' so that it is visibly finite over T' is the substance of the argument. H2.
